description:
A randonnée is an organized, long distance, timed riding event. It isn't a race, but participants do them to test oneself against the clock, the weather, and a challenging route. These events require you to carry your own gear (inner tubes, snacks, extra clothing) with you. So any good randonneuring bike basically needs to be an efficient and reliable road bike than can safely carry basic essentials.

If timed bike rides that sometimes run through the night, aren't your cup of tea, why should you even consider Grand Randonneur beyond it classic good looks? If you enjoy long road rides and love the convenience of a front handlebar bag or even prefer front pannier bags, this is one of the only production frames that is designed to improve the experience of carry weight on the front of the bike. Its low trail geometry delivers stable (less jerky and floppy) steering when loaded up , which is great for credit card touring, longer group rides, and even commuting. Doesn't your commute sometimes feel like a timed bike ride?

The version 3 of the "Grando" makes quite a few updates.

The geometry is still low trail in the front, but we have tried to make the low trail aspects less pronounced than in version 1 and 2.

We have tweaked the tubing mix to add stiffness at the bottom bracket, while keeping this frame one of our lighter models. Most sizes have a standard 25.4mm OD top tube, but sizes 58cm and up have more oversized tubes to better match up with larger riders.

We have modernized parts of it: Adding IS disc mounts and thru-axle hub compatibility.

And of course everyone wants slightly more tire clearance.

With its skinny steel tubes and 1" threaded lugged crown fork it still has the look of a vintage road bike.

Designed for 650b wheels

(Max. fender width: 50mm)

Rear rack and fender eyelets

Pump peg at headtube

Two sets of water bosses

Compatible with downtube shifters

This type of bike rides best with a front load. You can ride it unloaded, but it will take time to get used to the steering qualities of a low trail geometry.

Start with the customer – find out what they want and give it to them.
